correctness.rationale: The greedy Zeckendorf recurrence s(F_k+t)=1+s(t) for 0<=t<F_(k-1), together with induction on Fibonacci indices, yields exact boundary arrays for k=2r: s(F_k−4..−1)=(r−1,r−2,r−1,r−1) and k=2r+1: (r−1,r−1,r−1,r), and above a boundary s(F_k+j)=(1,2,2,2,3) for j=0..4. Their four crossing-offset cases close a strong induction proving: when s(n),s(n+2),s(n+4) have the same parity, an adjacent pair are equal. For odd Zeckendorf–Niven triples the summand counts must be odd divisors; equal adjacent counts divide 2, so equal 1 and the two numbers are Fibonacci values 2 apart, forcing candidates n=1,3. n3 fails because s(7)=2∤7; n1 yields (1,3,5). Independent greedy Zeckendorf implementation tested every n from 0 through 999999 for the parity lemma and all odd triples in that range, finding no parity violation and only n1; these tests are ancillary to the unrestricted induction.

evidence: Lao et al. arXiv:2606.24006 Theorem4.3 bounds length≥8; Theorem4.4 constructs length5.
Odd-length3 impossibility for n>1 is neither one of these statements nor a corollary of an eight-term classification.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Lao et al. prove long step-two progressions exist (with even starts) and constrain runs of length at least eight to a particular even progression. That is not a logical statement about length-three odd starts: a three-term run need not extend to eight terms. General Fibonacci automaticity alone does not directly yield the stated parity-rigidity lemma without a proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A theorem characterizing all step-two length≥8 runs does not say whether length3 at odd starts is possible: it leaves short runs completely open. The new parity-equality forced by equal parity of the three Zeckendorf digit sums, plus odd-divisibility, is the missing implication. The result is strictly narrower in length but orthogonal in start parity to existing broad existence results.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Zeckendorf–Niven is also called Fibonacci-summand-count Harshad; canonical Zeckendorf digits are nonconsecutive Fibonacci-place digits. The odd step-two three-term sequence is different from ordinary consecutive Zeckendorf–Niven runs (difference 1) and from an arbitrary longer progression with even start. The parity rigidity proposition is an extra statement about digit sums regardless of divisibility.

value.rationale: The Zeckendorf digit-sum divisibility analogue of Niven numbers is a natural digital-arithmetic object with known long step-two progressions. The result supplies a complete, sharply different odd-start length-three phenomenon and a reusable infinite parity-rigidity lemma, not merely a tabulation of a handful of values.
